items.title: 52300_Trummy Young oral history interview
items.q: And there was a guy down there, Georgia Red, he's a trombone player.

ctx.x: Yeah, well, I knew -- I knew a few musicians around Savannah and they played instruments. And they didn't play them very well but they played them, you know. And I used to hang around some of these musicians. I was just a kid.

And they'd let you pick up their horn and fool around with it, you know. And there was a guy down there, Georgia Red, he's a trombone player. And I used to fool -- he didn't play very good. But he lived in my neighborhood. So -- and he'd come around there. And we had a piano at my house. And a couple of guys played piano pretty good. My sister used to study piano. Came around there and they would play and eat. Some of them with their instruments would get right there and fool around with their instruments.

But there were really not many good players around there. The best musicians around Savannah at that time to me were the old blues players that didn't know anything about what they were doing, but they played. You know, they didn't -- as far as knowing, they didn't know what they were doing. But it sounded good. They had a knack for doing what -- and the blues players then were far ahead of other players back at that time. You know, because it was their own thing, you know. They weren't copying nobody, just how…
